Subject: Kiosk renewal + ops pulse: timeline & QBR scheduling

Alex —

Thanks again for the productive check-in last week. As Kiosk approaches the end of the current term (Nov 15), I want to kick off a short renewal & expansion coordination thread to align timelines, stakeholders, and next steps. High-level items we should cover: 

- Confirm target term and any preferred start/end adjustments (you mentioned Nov 15 vs Nov 30)
- Discuss planned capacity bump for holiday peak (estimated 2.5x burst for 6 weeks)
- Procurement path / PO and contract owner at Kiosk
- Schedule a QBR to review usage, hit the SLA/pricing ask, and run through the mutual action plan

Attached: Kiosk_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (proposed milestones) and Redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (SOW + pricing appendix).

Can you introduce your procurement contact (if different from procurement@kiosk.ai) and share 2 windows next week for a 45m QBR? Monica and Karthik will join from our side — Monica to review capacity/staffing; Karthik to discuss commercial options. Marissa will own onboarding logistics.

Next steps from our side: we’ll run a quick capacity read and propose a burst-sizing recommendation by Monday.

Thanks,

Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

Subject: Re: Kiosk renewal + ops pulse: timeline & QBR scheduling

Hi Rishi —

Appreciate the note and the docs. A couple quick answers:

- Term: We prefer to keep Nov 15 as the effective end date but are flexible on an administrative extension to Nov 30 if it helps the billing cadence.
- Burst: The estimate (2.5x for 6 weeks) sounds about right; finance will want a clear delta on committed baseline vs burst usage so we can model costs.
- Procurement: procurement@kiosk.ai is the right mailbox; Leah (CC’d) is our product lead and will join the QBR for the technical discussion.

QBR windows: Tue 8/18 10:00–10:45 PT or Wed 8/19 14:00–14:45 PT work for us. If those are tight, we can push to the following week.

Procurement asks: a redline-friendly SOW, an appendix listing committed baseline/overage rates, and an estimate of the onramp ramp-day staffing needs. Can you confirm whether the SOW supports a DocuSign route?

Thanks — Alex
VP Product | Kiosk.ai

Alex / team —

Thanks for the quick reply and the QBR windows. I’ll be on the 8/18 10:00 PT call (please send calendar invite for that slot). Preliminary notes from an ops perspective: 

- Baseline: current provisioned throughput should cover typical weekdays; to handle a 2.5x holiday burst we recommend a staged uplift: 1.5x in month 1, 2.0x in month 2, then 2.5x for peak weeks. This helps reduce immediate commit size while giving predictability.
- Staffing: estimated additional SRE on-call coverage of 0.4 FTE during peak (approx 2 weeks pre-peak + 6 weeks peak).
- Quantization/optimizations: we can evaluate a quantized instance mix to lower token costs for non-latency-critical flows.

I’ve attached a short capacity recommendation workbook (capacity_recommendation_v3.xlsx) with numbers mapped to the SOW appendix; Karthik — can you add a pricing sketch before the QBR? Rishi, I suggest we surface two commercial options: (A) committed baseline + capped burst overage, (B) staircase commit with seasonal additive credits.

Monica
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
